advanced_marks_vs_rank.basis: CRL. JIC Report 2023 sec 6.6. CRL size 26,321; last CRL rank scored 86 (= CRL cutoff 86/360). Topper 341/360. Built from the official table 'Aggregate Total Marks with Different Ranks in CRL' (the aggregate score of the candidate at CRL rank 1, 101, 201, ...). A subset of those points was used; each band runs from one mark above the next point's score up to this point's score, ranks from this point's rank to one below the next point's rank. Tied scores mean edge ranks are approximate to within ~100.

uncertainties: NTA does not publish marks-vs-percentile tables. Every JEE Main marks-to-percentile table here is either a coaching compilation or Claude's average of coaching shift-wise data. Percentile is normalised per shift, and the same marks gave very different percentiles in different shifts: in Jan 2025 the 99th percentile needed 148 to 200 marks; in Apr 2025, 173 to 203; in Jan 2026, 155 to 171.

Coaching sites recycle the same tables under different year labels. The 'BYJU'S 2023' marks/percentile table is identical to Vedantu's '2025' table and Allen's unlabelled table. Careers360's percentile-rank tables all fit rank = (100 - p) x N / 100 exactly, but with a different N in each: its '2026' table uses N = 14,75,103 (NTA's 2025 count), its '2025' table N ~ 14.15 lakh (2024's count), its '2024' table N ~ 10.98 lakh, and BYJU'S '2023' N ~ 9.21 lakh. Their rank columns are therefore formula outputs, not observed ranks, and their year labels are unreliable. So only formula estimates using official NTA candidate counts are included as main_percentile_vs_rank.

Observed 2025 CRL ranks are worse than the formula gives. CollegePravesh data points, seen only in a search-result excerpt because the page blocks automated fetching: 99.41 percentile = rank 9,100; 99.34 = 10,137; 99.25 = 11,596; 99.05 = 14,717. The formula with N = 14,75,103 gives 8,703; 9,736; 11,063; 14,013, about 4-5% better. Treat formula ranks as optimistic.

Careers360's own 'JEE Main 2025 Marks vs Percentile vs Rank' table was excluded because it is internally inconsistent: overlapping bands (201-222 vs 222-240, 161-180 vs 180-200), the same percentile upper bound in two bands, and the typo rank '210010'. Vedantu's '2026' marks/percentile table was excluded because its percentile ranges run in the wrong direction inside bands. henceprove.com's 2023-2025 table was excluded as implausible (it gives 100 marks = ~50 percentile).

No post-result shift-wise marks-vs-percentile data was found for JEE Main 2024 (Jan or Apr). The 2024 Jan table is Sri Chaitanya's pre-result prediction. Another figure, 27 Jan S1 needing 236 marks for 99 percentile, appeared only in search excerpts from Scribd and Collegedunia (not fetchable) and conflicts with Sri Chaitanya's 190. No 2024 Apr or 2023 per-session table was found.

The 2026 Apr session table comes from jeepredictor.in's model of student-reported scores, not NTA data. Careers360's Apr 2026 shift ranges (exact 5-mark steps with identical 20-mark gaps across all shifts) looked synthetic and were not used. jeepredictor.in's own Jan 2026 average for the 99th percentile (162) matches the Careers360-derived average used here (162).
Rank formula N for 2024 (14,15,110) and 2026 (15,38,474, with a variant of 15,38,468) come from news reports of NTA releases. The NTA PDFs were opened only for 2023 and 2025.

JEE Advanced 2023-2025 tables are official (JIC reports). Coaching Advanced tables disagree badly. cracku.in's 2026 'expected' table puts 300-329 marks at ranks 11-100 and lists wrong toppers (2024 as 348; official 355). eSaral's 2023 and 2024 tables contradict the official reports (e.g. 2023 rank 501 at 192 marks vs official 242). Careers360's 2026 'expected' Advanced table runs to rank 2.4 lakh and is not a CRL table. None were used.

JEE Advanced 2026 has only an official top-10 band (311-330 marks gives CRL 1-10) plus the CRL cutoff (92/360). The full 2026 marks-vs-rank table should appear in the JIC Report 2026 at jeeadv.ac.in/reports/ once published. The 2026 CRL cutoff (92) is much higher than 2025's (74), so the 2025 table cannot be reused unchanged for 2026.
JEE Advanced max marks were 360 in all four years (2023-2026), confirmed in the official reports and press releases. Qualifying cutoffs vary by year: CRL 86 (2023), 109 (2024), 74 (2025), 92 (2026).
